While EMT simulations were used to characterize detailed GFM behaviors such as angle-persistence, voltage- strengthening, and current-limit dynamics, positive-sequence models were benchmarked against these EMT results to ensure consistency during voltage and frequency events. Although full field demonstration was not reached within BP1, this alignment ensures that planning models can be used reliably for future impact studies and for pre-commissioning coordination with the transmission operator. Finally, Task 8 synthesized key observations from system-level studies into practical guidance for future demonstration. This included identification of events appropriate for field testing, recommended measurement requirements, and operational considerations for enabling GFM modes under real-world system variability. These deliverables provide a structured basis for the system-level evaluation that would occur in BP2 and reduce technical uncertainty associated with first-of-kind mixed- resource GFM operation at the scale of the Wheatridge hybrid plant. Through these modeling and validation activities, Task 8 delivered a system-level understanding of GFM behavior that is tightly linked to practical implementation constraints and planning-model considerations. The results establish a technically defensible baseline for future GFM commissioning and set the analytical foundation for evaluating GFM services in large hybrid facilities under realistic grid conditions. 8. Significant Accomplishments and Conclusions: 8.1 Significant Technical Accomplishments During Budget Period 1, the project delivered the analytical, modeling, validation, and engineering groundwork necessary to prepare for grid-forming (GFM) operation in a multi-technology hybrid plant. Major accomplishments include: (1) Development of a Comprehensive GFM Performance Framework The team established a full suite of grid-forming performance metrics, including angle strength, voltage strength, damping, inertial response, current-limiting behavior, and active/reactive voltage regulation. This framework provides consistent definitions, measurement criteria, and evaluation methods for use in EMT studies, positive-sequence modeling, HIL testing, and future field measurements. Page 22 of 36 Award Number: DE-EE0010651 Recipient Name: Portland General Electric (2) Multi-Stage EMT Validation of GFM Capabilities Three rounds of EMT studies characterized GFM behavior under weak-grid operation, large phase-angle disturbances, voltage steps, frequency events, and mixed GFM/GFL conditions. These studies confirmed expected GFM properties, angle regulation, voltage stiffness, and enhanced disturbance recovery, and identified parameter ranges necessary for stable operation within the Wheatridge plant. (3) High-Fidelity EMT Models and Foundational Positive-Sequence Model Work Inverter-level EMT models were completed for GFM BESS, GFM wind turbines, GFL wind, and solar, including plant-level supervisory controls. Initial work was completed toward a positive-sequence model structure for GFM Type-3 wind turbines, representing an essential step toward interconnection-level studies and aligning with SOPO Task 8 requirements. (4) Real-Time Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) Testbed Development A real-time HIL environment was constructed and validated to support firmware-level controller testing, tuning preparation, and evaluation of GFM/GFL interaction under dynamic disturbances not easily replicated in EMT simulations. Timing, synchronization, and stability were confirmed for early-stage GFM control evaluation. (5) Completion of Site Measurement Infrastructure High-speed measurement equipment (PPMS/DDR) was installed and operational at the Wheatridge site, consistent with Task 7. Communication paths, data logging, and configuration settings were validated in preparation for future field disturbances and performance verification. (6)
